title: SIU clears police in fatal April shooting; Man died of self-inflicted gunshot wound to head after chase
article: The 43-year-old Montreal man who was shot by Ottawa police officers after leading them on a high-speed highway chase in April died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head, according to Ontario's Special Investigations Unit.

The SIU -- the civilian agency that investigates incidents involving police that result in serious injury or death -- cleared three Ottawa police officers of any wrongdoing after concluding an investigation into the shooting.
Police chased Richard Bastien eastbound on Highway 417 at around 5:30 p.m. on April 22, after he allegedly shot and tried to kill his former boss at the latter's Carp-area home.
According to the SIU, Bastien pulled over near Walkley Road, got out of his car and pointed a revolver at one of the three officers on the scene.
An officer who was still sitting in his cruiser then shot at Bastien "a number of times."

"Almost simultaneously, Mr. Bastien shot himself in the area of his left temple. According to the autopsy, the self-inflicted wound, and not the wound inflicted by the officer, was the fatal one," SIU director Ian Scott said in a news release.
Bastien died in hospital two days after the shooting.

Rainer Elsner, 65, was shot in the back, arm and head after Bastien allegedly broke into his home. Elsner, a denturist, told his neighbour and police that the gunman was a former employee he had accused of forging cheques.
"The officer had reasonable grounds to believe that Mr. Bastien might shoot either him or another officer, and accordingly was justified in shooting," Scott said.
"The officer's reasonable belief was based upon the receipt of credible information that Mr. Bastien had just shot someone, was armed, and was pointing a firearm at him."
Though Bastien pointed his gun at the officers, he did not shoot at them, the SIU said.
Bastien's sister-in-law, Joanne, said Friday that the family had no comment.
Before the incident involving Bastien, Ottawa police had only shot two people in the preceding 10 years.

Bastien's was one of four shootings involving Ottawa police officers in a period of six months. The SIU has cleared the officers involved in three of the shootings. The fourth, which occurred on June 3 when officers executing a drug-related search warrant at a ByWard Market apartment shot a 36-year-old man in the leg, remains under investigation.
